install_symbols.why: one instance (ID 01): the CSD's ZC@ID@FILE and ZC@ID@KEY are ZC01FILE and ZC01KEY (EIBTRNID(3:2) names them)

vsam.why: Source/ZECSFILE.idcams: INDEXED KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(100 32700); the CSD's DEFINE FILE(ZC@ID@FILE) DSNAME is @ECS_HLQ@.ZC@ID@FILE.@ENVIRONMENT@ and the engine does not read the IDCAMS job as a define. The CSD defines it RECORDFORMAT(V); every record the case seeds is the one length reclen, so the stub's fixed-length records stand in (the program reads INTO ZF-RECORD, 32700 bytes)

Source/ZECSKEY.idcams: INDEXED KEYS(255 0) RECORDSIZE(512 512); the CSD's DEFINE FILE(ZC@ID@KEY) DSNAME is @ECS_HLQ@.ZC@ID@KEY.@ENVIRONMENT@, not read as a define (RECORDFORMAT(V) there, fixed 512-byte records in the stub)

notes: zECS's HTTP service for one instance (ZECS001), a POST of a new key on an empty cache. 4000-GET-COUNTER calls ZUIDSTCK for THE-TOD and 4120-WRITE-KEY keeps THE-TOD(1:6) as the key record's unique-ID prefix ZK-ZF-IDN. The TOD is a stated input of the run (register X47, #5945): the case states two different ones, and both runtimes write a key record that differs by exactly those six bytes.

scenarios.name: post-tod-a
scenarios.why: POST key1 with the TOD 0001020304050607...: the key record is written with ZK-ZF-IDN X'000102030405' and the file record under it

scenarios.name: post-tod-b
scenarios.why: the same POST with the TOD D4A3C1B2E5F60718...: the same task, the key record's ZK-ZF-IDN is X'D4A3C1B2E5F6'
